newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's GFM signs Pacific-North railroad contract.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's GFM signs Pacific-North railroad contract.

text.p: Mexican rail company Grupo Ferroviaria Mexicana (GFM) said on Monday it had signed a multi-billion peso deal with the government giving it 100 percent control of the Pacific-North rail line.

"The Federal Government and Grupo Ferroviario Mexico today formalized the contract for the deal involving 100 percent of the shares of the Pacific-North rail line for a sum of 3.94 billion pesos," the statement said.
GFM, a consortium consisting of Grupo Mexico SA Union Pacific and ICA SA, obtained 100 percent of the shares of Pacific-North on July 4 after bidding $527 million.
GFM has promised to invest $425 million in the line over the next five years.

It also won the concession to run the Chihuahua-Pacific railroad, and on Monday it said it intended to retain its concession for the Ojinaga-Topolobampo line that runs from the Pacific coast to Texas. ((--Caroline Brothers, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7905))
